facts.label: Cross-source distinctions and conflicts
facts.text: 1. Leverage definitions differ. The Q3 release defines its ratio as Leverage ratio is defined as net debt divided by last twelve months adjusted EBITDA (EX-99.1 Q3 page:21) and reports Net debt was $10,656m at the end of Q3, with a leverage ratio of 4.6x (3.7x at December 31, 2025) (page:11). The covenant in the 10-K is the ratio of consolidated net borrowings to consolidated EBITDA as defined therein (the net total leverage ratio) is not greater than 5.20:1 on a bi-annual basis (10-K page:128). The 10-Q warns that The definition of Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt agreements. (10-Q Q3 page:71). Effect: the release ratio and the covenant ratio are not comparable, and the sources print no covenant ratio value. 2. Covenant changes after quarter end. The Q3 10-Q (page:42) says the amendment replaces the net total leverage financial covenant with a net first lien leverage financial covenant and the financial covenant level increased to 5.70:1.00. The 5.20:1 level in the 10-K applies to the pre-amendment test only. No source prints a first lien net leverage figure. 3. Facility size statements are not reconciled. The Q3 release says the refinancing is increasing the overall facility size by approximately $240m and extending the maturity date from November 2028 to May 2032 (page:12). The Q3 10-Q says the committed revolving facility has been increased to $1.86 billion (page:75), and the 10-K described the Group’s $1.48 billion (£1.1 billion) committed revolving credit facility (page:125). The release figure covers an undefined set of facilities; the sources do not show how it relates to the revolver figures. Effect: CP-2 must use the filing figures and treat the release figure as unreconciled. 4. Maturity table pre-dates the amendment. The Q3 repayment schedule (10-Q Q3 page:26) is stated as of September 30, 2026, and the amendment of October 30, 2026 extends the term A and revolving maturities to May 3, 2032 (page:42). The schedule therefore no longer matches the post-amendment structure for the term A and revolver amounts it places in 2028; the pro forma schedule is not supplied. 5. Net debt basis. The release defines net debt as total debt, excluding premiums, discounts, and deferred financing expense, and the effect of foreign exchange that is economically hedged less cash (EX-99.1 Q3 page:20); the 10-Q prints Total debt and Total debt principal including accrued interest on different bases (10-Q Q3 page:26). The three bases are not reconciled in the sources. 6. Legal provision scope. The 10-Q contingency note (page:40) gives a Fast Code provision of $109 million (A$157.5 million), while the Adjusted EBITDA add-back for the quarter is $105 million relates to a provision recognized to facilitate a potential resolution of the Fast Code Class Action, partially offset by an adjustment in connection with the Indian GST matter (page:16). These are different scopes, not a conflict, and must not be added or substituted. 7. Stated period labels. Release highlights and the 10-Q use the same Q3 2026 figures for revenue and net loss (3,874 and (1,148) on the Q3 10-Q page:6 and release page:22). Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of 360 is a release figure (EX-99.1 Q3 page:24); the 10-Q segment note gives segment totals for the quarter and nine months (10-Q Q3 page:14).

facts.label: Evidence assessment by need
facts.text: - Statements and periods. Evidence: the Q3 10-Q prints Three months ended September 30, Nine months ended September 30, columns for 2026 and 2025 (page:6), and the 10-K prints three fiscal years. Risk: the cash flow statement is nine months only, so quarterly cash items rest on the release's subtraction. Consequence: CP-1 can build discrete quarters for income items from the three 10-Qs and releases, and must label the derived cash-flow quarter as management-derived. - Debt and liquidity. Evidence: the latest debt table lists every facility and note series with principal and carrying value; the revolver note states The Group had an undrawn revolving credit commitment of $782 million (£590 million) as of September 30, 2026 and $13 million (£10 million) reserved for guarantees (10-Q Q3 page:27). Risk: the amendment text is only summarised, and letters of credit other than the guarantee reserve are not tabulated against the revolver. Consequence: CP-2 can compute liquidity at September 30, 2026 from printed inputs and must state the pro forma revolver as a subsequent event. - Claims outside debt. Evidence: operating leases (10-Q Q3 page:75: the Group had operating lease obligations of $559 million with $142 million payable within 12 months), purchase obligations (page:75: totaled $4,998 million), bank guarantees (page:38: The maximum amount of the guarantees as of September 30, 2026 was $620 million), the Fox option (10-K page:132: Fox has until December 2030 to exercise the Fox Option; fair value Fox Option liability — — 100 100 at 10-Q Q3 page:33), redeemable non-controlling interests and litigation and tax matters (10-Q Q3 pages 38 to 42). Risk: the 10-K lease note describes Substantially all leases are long-term operating leases and the 10-Qs carry no lease maturity table. Consequence: CP-2 can set out these claims with their locators; lease maturities are available at December 31, 2025 only. - Latest quarter and after. Evidence: Brazil operations are currently ceased after the measure announced September 25, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:14); the UKI restructuring plan of October 20, 2026 (page:42); the amendment of October 30, 2026 (page:42); a paused repurchase programme (page:75); revised 2026 guidance (EX-99.1 Q3 page:12). Risk: guidance is management's claim and the restructuring cost is an estimate range. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 can cover the events up to the cutoff; none is dated after November 5, 2026.

rows.label: The annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases are enough to run all four selected modules on the consolidated group, each with stated limits. Nothing blocks the work.
Audited annual statements and three 2026 interim reports are present, with debt, segment, cash flow and covenant text.
The October 2026 credit agreement amendment is described only in a note and a release, not supplied as a document.
Covenant compliance is stated, but no covenant ratio values are printed, and the company's own leverage ratio uses a different definition.
Brazil operations have ceased, and legal and tax matters with disclosed amounts are reported, some with no provision.
Sources are text extractions only. No investor presentations, ratings or market quotes are supplied.
No executed credit agreement, indentures, officer's certificates or First Amendment and Restatement Agreement. Terms are known from filing summaries only.

Covenant ratio values are not printed; only the Group was in compliance with all debt covenants (10-Q Q3 page:27). The pre-amendment level was 5.20:1 and the post-amendment first lien level is 5.70:1, with different definitions.
Guarantor list and the subsidiary list (Exhibit 21.1) are not supplied.

The Q3 debt table prints no interest rates, issuers, guarantors or security. Rates and security come from the 10-K at December 31, 2025. Whether any rate changed in 2026 is not shown for the term loans, other than the post-amendment margin range of 1.40% to 2.00% for term A and revolver loans.
Pro forma maturity schedule after the amendment is not supplied; the Q3 schedule is pre-amendment.
Facility-size statements are not reconciled (release approximately $240m increase; 10-Q revolver $1.86 billion).

Letters of credit are mentioned only inside the bank guarantee note (third-party letter of credit facilities, 10-Q Q3 page:38), with a total guarantee amount and no split by facility. Whether any draws on the revolver is not stated; the only printed revolver deduction is a $13 million (£10 million) reservation for guarantees (10-Q Q3 page:27).
Cash flows in the 10-Qs are year-to-date only; quarterly cash flows are management-derived in the release. The Q3 10-Q cash flow caption reads "decrease" over positive amounts.

Segment comparatives may have been recast for customer transfers between regions during 2026 (beginning April 1, 2026, PokerStars’ North America operations formed part of the US region, 10-Q Q3 page:14). The sources do not say whether FY2025 segment figures were recast.

No Q4 2025 earnings release, no investor presentations, no market quotes and no peer data. The Q3 10-Q says the post-amendment margin depends on corporate ratings from Moody’s, S&P and Fitch (page:42), but no rating is stated in any source, and the context ratings field is blank.
The extraction was not compared with the filed HTML or XBRL; no chart or image content was inspected.
The context lists the country as Netherlands; the filings state Ireland.
Fox option: the option price and fair value are disclosed, but the Fox option agreement is not supplied; the 10-K states the exercise window to December 2030.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The consolidated financial base is complete enough to use: audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim sets, a segment note, an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation in every period and a debt note at each quarter end are all located. The picture they give is of a group whose total debt rose by 5,530 in 2025 (6,736 to 12,266, C13), with the proceeds of the 2025 term loan and note issues used to repay the bridge loans for the Snai acquisition and the Boyd transaction (10-K page:126), and whose earnings have since weakened. Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 is 1,499 against 2,013 for nine months 2025, driven by the US segment (241 against 612) and a higher UK gaming duty in International, while total debt is almost flat (12,313 at September 30, 2026 against 12,266 at December 31, 2025). Calculated total debt to Adjusted EBITDA therefore rises from 4.31x at FY2025 to 5.28x on a last-twelve-month basis, and the company's own net leverage ratio moves from 3.7x to 4.6x. Cash interest cover on the same basis falls from 5.36x to 3.67x.

facts.text: Three features limit the view. First, the headline measure is the company's Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes share-based compensation, restructuring, legal loss contingencies, transaction costs and impairment; the 10-Q says its definition may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt agreements. Second, the last-twelve-month figures are calculated from annual and year-to-date data, and the segment comparatives for 2025 appear not to be recast for the 2026 customer transfers between regions. Third, cash flow from operations moves with player deposit balances, which are not the Group's own cash. The figures should be read as a documented reported base with calculated overlays, not as covenant tests.

The 10-K notes that Beginning January 1, 2024, the Group revised its definition of Adjusted EBITDA (page:99); FY2024 and FY2023 figures in the 10-K are on the revised basis, and no earlier basis is supplied. - Items excluded in the nine months to September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:72): share-based compensation 176, transaction fees 32, restructuring and integration costs 254, legal loss contingencies 200 and impairment 873. The restructuring programmes are expected to run until 2029 (page:73), so the restructuring add-back is recurring in practice. Cash cost of the UKI restructuring, $80 million to $90 million pre-tax, is announced after quarter end (page:42) and is not in any period shown. - Operating lease cost is inside Adjusted EBITDA (it is an operating expense), and operating lease liabilities sit outside debt. This answer uses carrying total debt less unrestricted cash, so its net debt (10,605) is lower than the release's (10,656) by 51. facts.label: Evidence assessment
facts.text: - Leverage. Evidence: total debt 12,313 at September 30, 2026 against 12,266 at December 31, 2025 (Total debt 12,313 12,266, Q3 10-Q page:26), while LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 2,331 against 2,845. Mechanism: the 2025 acquisition debt is in place for the full period, and earnings fell in the US segment (241 against 612 for nine months) and from the UK gaming duty in International (Q3 10-Q page:70: an increase of remote gaming tax in UK). Consequence: calculated total leverage rose by about one turn between FY2025 and Q3 2026, and the company itself targets 2.0 - 2.5x (Q3 release page:12). - Cover. Evidence: cash interest paid 636 over the last twelve months against 531 in FY2025. Mechanism: a full year of interest on the notes due 2031 and Term Loan B due 2032 issued in 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:53: a full quarter of interest on the Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and the USD First Lien Term Loan B due 2032 issued in August 2025). Consequence: cover on cash interest fell from 5.36x to 3.67x, and the next twelve months carry $696 million payable within 12 months net of hedging of scheduled interest (Q3 10-Q page:74). - Cash flow. Evidence: free cash flow of 377 for 9M 2026 against 269 for 9M 2025, but 201 against 396 once player deposit movements are removed. Mechanism: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was lifted by player funds (176) and higher accrued legal and gaming duty liabilities (Q3 10-Q page:76). Consequence: the improvement in reported free cash flow is not evidence of stronger underlying cash generation; share repurchases of 543 over the last twelve months exceeded free cash flow of 515, and the programme is now paused (Q3 10-Q page:75). - Liquidity. Evidence: cash 1,708 and undrawn revolver commitments 782 at September 30, 2026. Mechanism: the revolver was drawn to fund operations and repayments (drew £1,208 million ($1,621 million), Q3 10-Q page:27). Consequence: the sterling revolver headroom fell from 1,185 at March 31, 2026 to 782; the post-amendment commitment is larger, but its undrawn amount is not supplied. - Earnings quality. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,499 for 9M 2026 against an operating loss of 1,256 and net loss of 1,235. Mechanism: impairment of 873 on Brazil, legal loss contingencies of 200 and restructuring of 254 are excluded. Consequence: cash costs among those items (legal settlements, restructuring severance) will reduce free cash flow in later periods even though they do not reduce Adjusted EBITDA. - Guidance context (management claim). The Q3 release gives 2026 guidance midpoints of revenue $17.61bn and Adjusted EBITDA $2.495bn (page:12). Subtracting the nine-month figures implies fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of about 996 and revenue of about 5,106 (C12). This is management's guidance, not a forecast built here, and it assumes the nine-month figures in this answer.

Mechanism: the 2025 acquisition debt is in place for the full period, and earnings fell in the US segment (241 against 612 for nine months) and from the UK gaming duty in International (Q3 10-Q `page:70`: `an increase of remote gaming tax in UK`). Consequence: calculated total leverage rose by about one turn between FY2025 and Q3 2026, and the company itself targets `2.0 - 2.5x` (Q3 release `page:12`).

- **Cover.** Evidence: cash interest paid 636 over the last twelve months against 531 in FY2025. Mechanism: a full year of interest on the notes due 2031 and Term Loan B due 2032 issued in 2025 (Q3 10-Q `page:53`: `a full quarter of interest on the Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and the USD First Lien Term Loan B due 2032 issued in August 2025`). Consequence: cover on cash interest fell from 5.36x to 3.67x, and the next twelve months carry `$696 million payable within 12 months net of hedging` of scheduled interest (Q3 10-Q `page:74`).

- **Cash flow.** Evidence: free cash flow of 377 for 9M 2026 against 269 for 9M 2025, but 201 against 396 once player deposit movements are removed. Mechanism: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was lifted by player funds (176) and higher accrued legal and gaming duty liabilities (Q3 10-Q `page:76`). Consequence: the improvement in reported free cash flow is not evidence of stronger underlying cash generation; share repurchases of 543 over the last twelve months exceeded free cash flow of 515, and the programme is now paused (Q3 10-Q `page:75`).

- **Liquidity.** Evidence: cash 1,708 and undrawn revolver commitments 782 at September 30, 2026. Mechanism: the revolver was drawn to fund operations and repayments (`drew £1,208 million ($1,621 million)`, Q3 10-Q `page:27`). Consequence: the sterling revolver headroom fell from 1,185 at March 31, 2026 to 782; the post-amendment commitment is larger, but its undrawn amount is not supplied.

- **Earnings quality.** Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,499 for 9M 2026 against an operating loss of 1,256 and net loss of 1,235. Mechanism: impairment of 873 on Brazil, legal loss contingencies of 200 and restructuring of 254 are excluded. Consequence: cash costs among those items (legal settlements, restructuring severance) will reduce free cash flow in later periods even though they do not reduce Adjusted EBITDA.

- **Guidance context (management claim).** The Q3 release gives 2026 guidance midpoints of revenue `$17.61bn` and Adjusted EBITDA `$2.495bn` (`page:12`). Subtracting the nine-month figures implies fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of about 996 and revenue of about 5,106 (C12). This is management's guidance, not a forecast built here, and it assumes the nine-month figures in this answer.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Flutter is an Ireland-incorporated, New York-headquartered online sports betting and iGaming group whose shares trade on the NYSE, with no sponsor and no controlling shareholder identified in the pack. Its revenue base is large and diversified by geography and product, with about 88% of FY2025 revenue earned online and the rest mainly through retail shops in the UK, Ireland, Italy and Serbia. Sportsbook revenue depends on the margin Flutter earns on fixed-odds bets, so it moves with sports results and with the sporting calendar; iGaming revenue is less dependent on the calendar. Both are exposed to gaming taxes that governments change at short notice, and the last year shows how fast this transmits: the UK raised remote gaming duty sharply in April 2026, Brazil's executive ban closed Flutter's Brazilian operations within days in September 2026, and India's 2025 ban ended Junglee. In India and Brazil Flutter took impairments, and in the UK it announced a restructuring.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The transaction history matters more to a creditor than the operating model. In 2025 the Group bought Snai in Italy, a 56% stake in NSX in Brazil, and the 5% of FanDuel held by Boyd, funding them with bridge loans refinanced by new term loan B and senior secured notes issued in June and August 2025. Total debt rose as a result (CP-1), while Brazil, bought with NSX in May 2025, was shut down within sixteen months and carries a large impairment. Management has since paused share repurchases to prioritise deleveraging and set a target leverage range, but earnings fell in 2026 and leverage is well above that range (CP-1). The contingent claim of Fox on FanDuel, a new CEO from October 1, 2026, a UKI restructuring and a credit agreement amendment on October 30, 2026 are subsequent changes that the debt and covenant modules must treat as post-period events. The amendment is known only from filing summaries.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In 2025 Flutter completed three acquisitions. On April 30, 2025 it bought 100% of Pluto (Italia) S.p.A, the holding company of Snai, for approximately $2.6 billion (€2.3 billion) (Q3 10-Q page:25). On May 14, 2025 it acquired a 56% interest in NSX for $674 million (BRL 3,799 million) with call and put options over the remainder (10-K page:9). It also acquired the 5% redeemable non-controlling interest in FanDuel held by Boyd for $1,553 million, taking its holding to 100% subject to the Fox option (10-K page:9). The accounting for Snai and NSX was finalised in the second quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:25, page:26). All three are documentary facts with status completed. The sources give acquisition terms only in these summaries, and no acquisition agreements are supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The acquisitions were financed in stages. A €2.5 billion bridge term loan drawn on April 29, 2025 funded Snai, and a $1.75 billion bridge drawn on July 30, 2025 funded the Boyd transaction (10-K page:125, page:126). They were repaid with new $1,250 million of Term Loan B due June 4, 2032 ($750 million on June 4 and $500 million on August 7, 2025) and with the 2031 senior secured notes issued in the same two tranches: $1,625 million of 5.875%, €850 million of 4.000% and £700 million of 6.125% (10-K page:126, page:127, page:128). The 2029 notes of $525 million at 6.375% and €500 million at 5.000% had been issued by Flutter Treasury DAC on April 29, 2024 (10-K page:127). The use of proceeds was repayment of the bridges, general corporate purposes and costs (10-K page:126). Liquidity effect: the debt table shows total debt rising over 2025 (CP-1), and the Group states it believes it has sufficient capacity through cash, internal funds and the revolver (Q3 10-Q page:74, a management statement).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: After the quarter, on October 30, 2026, the Group signed the First Amendment and Restatement Agreement to the November 2023 credit agreement (Q3 10-Q page:42). It extends the term A and revolver maturities to May 3, 2032, raises the revolver commitment to $1.86 billion with a US dollar base currency, redenominates term A into €382 million of term A2 loans and $1,374 million of term A3 loans, replaces the net total leverage covenant with a net first lien leverage covenant at 5.70:1.00, and prices term A and revolver loans at a margin of 1.40% to 2.00% set by corporate ratings (Q3 10-Q page:42). The revolver increase took effect on November 3, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:74). Status: completed, a subsequent event after September 30, 2026, described only in a note and in the Q3 release (page:12); the executed document is not supplied. The liquidity effect is an enlarged revolver, but the undrawn amount after the amendment is not disclosed. The Q3 release describes the facility increase as approximately $240m for the refinanced facilities without defining the set, which is not reconciled to the revolver figure (see conflicts).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: the revenue mix and regional split above (10-K page:10, page:11, page:12). Risk mechanic: revenue is spread over two segments, about 100 countries and many brands, so no single market is decisive; but sportsbook margin moves with sports results and tax rates are set by governments. Credit implication: diversification reduces the chance that one regulatory event impairs debt service, while regular tax and regulatory shocks reduce visibility of EBITDA and leave less room for leverage. Counter-evidence: the Brazil ban removed a region that was only 1% of FY2025 revenue, so geographic spread has so far limited revenue loss from individual bans. 2. Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: UK remote gaming duty from 21% to 40% (Q3 10-Q page:48) and the UKI restructuring of up to 1,400 jobs with charges of $80 million to $90 million (Q3 10-Q page:42). Risk mechanic: the duty is charged within cost of sales, which lowered International margin in 2026 (CP-1); mitigation costs are cash and excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. Credit implication: cash conversion falls before savings arrive, which weighs on interest cover in the next twelve months (CP-1: LTM cover on cash interest of 3.67x), and a further duty rise is scheduled for April 2027. 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: US 43% of FY2025 revenue and the seasonality statement (10-K page:11, page:12). Risk mechanic: US earnings depend on league calendars, state tax changes (North Carolina, where the sports betting tax rate increased from 18% to 23%, Q3 10-Q page:48) and prediction market investment. Credit implication: the segment that the Group calls its largest growth opportunity (We believe that our U.S. segment is the largest growth opportunity for the Group., Q3 10-Q page:47) currently produces the weakest earnings (CP-1: US Adjusted EBITDA of 241 for nine months 2026), so debt service relies on International for now. No customer concentration is disclosed. 4. Ownership, sponsor alignment and the Fox option. Evidence: no sponsor, no controlling holder identified; a Fox call option over 18.6% of FanDuel units at $4.8 billion as of December 31, 2025, compounding 5% a year, exercisable until December 2030 (10-K page:29, page:132). Risk mechanic: exercise requires cash payment to the Group, which would bring cash but reduce the Group's economic interest in FanDuel and could give Fox consent rights over matters such as acquisitions and debt incurrence if the former Fastball rights carry over; the filing says it has not been determined what specific rights Fox may receive. Credit implication: a possible deleveraging event with a loss of control over the largest growth asset; the timing is at Fox's choice and Fox must be licensed to exercise (10-K page:132). Fair value of the liability fell from 560 at December 31, 2025 to 100 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:33), a change that reflects management's valuation assumptions; the sources do not explain it in the pages read here. Counter-evidence: none logged. 5. Capital allocation and leverage tolerance. Evidence: debt-funded acquisitions, repurchases under the $5 billion programme, and the pause (Q3 10-Q page:75; Q3 release page:1). Risk mechanic: leverage at Q3 2026 is well above the stated range (CP-1), repurchases continued in the first half of 2026 before the pause (Q3 10-Q page:7, share repurchases in the first and second quarters), and the amendment raised the covenant level (5.70:1.00). Credit implication: leverage tolerance is high and the deleveraging path depends on earnings recovery and cash generation, which management has guided but not delivered (CP-1: net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 4.55x against the 2.0 to 2.5x target). 6. Key uncertainties. Legal and tax matters with amounts disclosed (Indian GST demand of ₹50.6 billion ($527 million) against a recorded $54 million, IRS proposed adjustments of about $181 million with no provision, and the Brazilian class action and NSX investigation; Q3 10-Q page:41, page:49, page:50) and the unavailability of the executed credit documents. Credit implication: these are claims outside the debt figure that could use cash or restrict financing; their size cannot be tied to covenant definitions from this pack.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Flutter's debt is adequately supported but stretched: the group is large, diversified and still cash generative, yet total debt to Adjusted EBITDA has risen to 5.28x and net debt to 4.55x, well above management's 2.0x to 2.5x target. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,477 million at September 30, 2026 and no sizeable maturity before 2029 once the October 2026 amendment is counted. The weakest point is earnings: higher UK gaming duty, the Brazil ban and weak US profit cut last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA to USD 2,331 million. What decides the outcome is whether cost actions and the buyback pause bring leverage down before further tax rises and legal settlements, and the covenant headroom for that cannot be measured from these sources.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Flutter's total debt of USD 12,313 million at September 30, 2026 is almost unchanged from USD 12,266 million at December 31, 2025, but last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 2,331 million from USD 2,845 million, so total debt to Adjusted EBITDA rose to 5.28x from 4.31x and net debt to 4.55x from 3.67x [CP-1]. The reason is earnings, not borrowing: nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,499 million against USD 2,013 million, with the US segment down to USD 241 million from USD 612 million and the UK remote gaming duty rising from 21% to 40% in April 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The Group's own leverage ratio is 4.6x against 3.7x at December 31, 2025 and a 2.0x to 2.5x target, and management has paused share repurchases to prioritise deleveraging.

The Group's own leverage ratio is 4.6x against 3.7x at December 31, 2025 and a 2.0x to 2.5x target, and management has paused share repurchases to prioritise deleveraging.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is the main support. Flutter held USD 1,708 million of unrestricted cash and USD 782 million of undrawn revolver commitments at September 30, 2026, USD 2,490 million in all, or USD 2,477 million if the USD 13 million guarantee reservation is also deducted. No debt matures within twelve months beyond USD 52 million of scheduled repayments, and the October 30, 2026 amendment extends the term A loans and the revolver to May 3, 2032, so the 2028 repayment of USD 2,681 million largely moves out, leaving about USD 51 million of 2028 amortisation on an indicative basis. The next large maturity is USD 1,143 million in 2029, then USD 3,692 million in 2030. The sterling revolver headroom did shrink during 2026, from USD 1,185 million at March 31 to USD 782 million at September 30.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Interest is the pressure point. Cash interest paid was USD 636 million over the last twelve months, and the Group expects USD 696 million of interest in the next twelve months net of hedging, which is 3.35x covered by last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA (calculated). facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Debt ranking and market signals complete the picture. Every funded instrument, the term loans, the revolver and the five senior secured note series, is secured first priority on the same collateral and guaranteed by the same group of guarantors, so creditors share one pool and there is no junior or unsecured debt to absorb losses first. The senior secured notes had a quoted fair value of about 94% of carrying amount at September 30, 2026, against about 100% at December 31, 2025 (calculated), which shows the market has repriced the credit even though the Group reports compliance with all covenants. The leverage covenant moved from a net total leverage level of 5.20:1 to a net first lien leverage level of 5.70:1.00, but no covenant ratio value is printed, so the Group's own ratio of 4.6x cannot be read as headroom.

Deleveraging intent (Management Language): the Group has paused share repurchases and committed to returning to 2.0x to 2.5x over the medium term, which management states and has not yet achieved [CP-1A, governance table]. Structure (Documentary Fact): there is no sponsor, no dividend since May 2020 and no documented priming, uptiering or collateral release [CP-1A, company profile and governance table]; the sources cannot test legal capacity for any of these because the credit documents are not supplied.

facts.label: Capital structure at September 30, 2026
facts.text: Notes on the table. The credit agreement is Term Loan A, Term Loan B and Revolving Credit Facility Agreement dated November 24, 2023 with J.P. Morgan SE as administrative agent (10-K page:125). The notes may be redeemed at prices set in the indenture from April 15, 2026 (2029 notes) and from April 15, 2027 (2031 notes) (10-K page:129); make-whole and equity-claw terms applied before those dates. Until April 15, 2027 the Issuer may redeem up to 40% of each 2031 series with equity proceeds at 105.875% (USD), 104% (EUR) and 106.125% (GBP) of principal (10-K page:129). The Group states the notes rank pari passu in right of payment with all existing and future senior debt of the Issuer that is not subordinated to the Notes (10-K page:128). After the October 30, 2026 amendment, term A2 loans of €382 million and term A3 loans of $1,374 million are outstanding, no sterling term A loans remain, and the revolver commitment is $1.86 billion in US dollars (10-Q Q3 page:42). Term A and revolver loans then bear Term SOFR, EURIBOR or SONIA plus 1.40% to 2.00% depending on the corporate ratings of Moody's, S&P and Fitch (10-Q Q3 page:42); no rating is stated in any source. Hedges: interest rate swaps with a notional of USD 1,489 million convert part of Term Loan B to fixed until June 30, 2027; a cross-currency swap of USD 525 million converts the 2029 USD notes to sterling until April 18, 2028; and fair value hedges of USD 500 million and USD 1,000 million relate to the 2031 USD notes until June 4, 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:28, page:29).

## Request

- Issuer: Flutter Entertainment plc (issuer id `flut`), as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05 (context). Reporting currency USD; current period Q3 2026 (quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026); prior period FY2025 (context).

- Execution: host session. The host read the pinned page text of each source and wrote this answer. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied public filings and earnings releases support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 for the consolidated Flutter group, and what remains blocked?

- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This handoff gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it normalizes, reconciles or calculates no figure.

- Perimeter: the reporting entity in every financial source is the registrant, Flutter Entertainment plc, and its subsidiaries ("the Group"), on a consolidated basis. Debt-level issuers (see the source register) are subsidiaries or co-obligors inside that perimeter; no separate statements for any of them are supplied.

- Statements: balance sheet `page:5` to `page:6`; comprehensive income (loss) `page:6` to `page:7`; equity statements `page:7` to `page:9`; cash flows `page:9` to `page:10` (nine months only).

- Notes: segments `page:13` to `page:18`; other income and interest `page:18` to `page:19`; business combinations `page:25` to `page:26`; long-term debt `page:26` to `page:27`; derivatives `page:27` to `page:31`; fair value `page:32` to `page:33`; commitments and contingencies `page:38` to `page:42`; subsequent events `page:42`.
- MD&A: results `page:43` onward; non-GAAP definitions `page:70` to `page:71`; liquidity, leases, purchase obligations and cash flows `page:74` to `page:76`.
- Units and currency: US dollars in millions; three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 with 2025 comparatives.

- Presentation fault to carry: the cash flow statement at `page:9` prints `NET DECREASE IN CASH, CASH EQUIVALENTS AND RESTRICTED CASH 137 138` with positive amounts under a "decrease" caption. Downstream use should take the caption-free beginning and ending balances on the same page and not infer a sign from the caption.
#### Earnings releases (three Exhibit 99.1 files)

- Family and authority: management-prepared press releases filed as Exhibit 99.1, not audited or reviewed statements. They supply attributed management narrative, guidance, non-GAAP reconciliations, the leverage ratio and net debt, and quarter-only cash flows.
- Q1 2026 (`EX-99.1_2026-05-06_d46069dex991.htm.jsonl`): `New York, May 6, 2026`; Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation `page:28`; guidance `page:15` to `page:16`.
- Q2 2026 (`EX-99.1_2026-08-05_d127369dex991.htm.jsonl`): `New York, August 5, 2026`; reconciliation `page:27`; guidance `page:13` to `page:14`.

- Q3 2026 (`EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d141532dex991.htm.jsonl`): `New York, November 4, 2026`; highlights and leverage ratio `page:1`; guidance `page:12`; non-GAAP definitions `page:20` to `page:21`; balance sheet `page:21` to `page:22`; cash flows `page:22` to `page:24`; reconciliation `page:24`. The quarter's cash flow statement is derived (`page:24`): `is derived by subtracting the cash flows from the six months ended June 30, 2026 from the cash flows for the nine months ended September 30, 2026`.
- Authority rule: where a release and a filing differ in definition or amount, the filing controls and the release is a supporting claim.
#### Context (`context`)

- User run settings. It leaves ratings, quotes, deal terms, valuation inputs, assumptions and research questions blank; blank values are not zero. It lists the country as `Netherlands`, while the filings give Ireland (`10-K page:1`: `Ireland 98-1782229`). The filings control; the context field is not issuer evidence.
### Debt and perimeter roles located in the sources

- Borrower group and agreement: `page:125` of the 10-K names the `TLA/TLB/RCF Agreement` of November 2023 with `J.P. Morgan SE as the administrative agent and Wilmington Trust (London) Limited, acting as the collateral agent`. The exhibit list (`10-K page:217`) names the borrowers, including PPB Treasury Unlimited Company, Betfair Interactive US Financing LLC, TSE Holdings Limited, FanDuel Group Financing LLC and Flutter Financing B.V.

- Notes issuer: `Flutter Treasury DAC (the “Issuer”)` issued the 2029 and 2031 senior secured notes (`10-K page:128`). Guarantors are described only generally: `guaranteed on a senior secured basis by the Group and certain of its subsidiaries (collectively, the “Guarantors”)` (`10-K page:128`). The guarantor list is not supplied.

- Facilities and series in the latest debt table (`10-Q Q3 page:26`): three first lien Term Loan A tranches due 2028, the revolving credit facility due 2028, Term Loan B due 2030, Term Loan B due 2032 and five senior secured note series. The table prints principal and carrying amounts but no rates, issuers or guarantors.

- Security: `first priority security interest (subject to permitted liens)` over shares held by an obligor in another obligor and, for United States obligors, substantially all United States assets (`10-K page:127`).
### Cross-source distinctions and conflicts

1. **Leverage definitions differ.** The Q3 release defines its ratio as `Leverage ratio is defined as net debt divided by last twelve months adjusted EBITDA` (`EX-99.1 Q3 page:21`) and reports `Net debt was $10,656m at the end of Q3, with a leverage ratio of 4.6x (3.7x at December 31, 2025)` (`page:11`). The covenant in the 10-K is `the ratio of consolidated net borrowings to consolidated EBITDA as defined therein (the net total leverage ratio) is not greater than 5.20:1 on a bi-annual basis` (`10-K page:128`). The 10-Q warns that `The definition of Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt agreements.` (`10-Q Q3 page:71`). Effect: the release ratio and the covenant ratio are not comparable, and the sources print no covenant ratio value.

2. **Covenant changes after quarter end.** The Q3 10-Q (`page:42`) says the amendment `replaces the net total leverage financial covenant with a net first lien leverage financial covenant and the financial covenant level increased to 5.70:1.00`. The 5.20:1 level in the 10-K applies to the pre-amendment test only. No source prints a first lien net leverage figure.

3. **Facility size statements are not reconciled.** The Q3 release says the refinancing is `increasing the overall facility size by approximately $240m and extending the maturity date from November 2028 to May 2032` (`page:12`). The Q3 10-Q says the committed revolving facility `has been increased to $1.86 billion` (`page:75`), and the 10-K described `the Group’s $1.48 billion (£1.1 billion) committed revolving credit facility` (`page:125`). The release figure covers an undefined set of facilities; the sources do not show how it relates to the revolver figures. Effect: CP-2 must use the filing figures and treat the release figure as unreconciled.

4. **Maturity table pre-dates the amendment.** The Q3 repayment schedule (`10-Q Q3 page:26`) is stated as of September 30, 2026, and the amendment of October 30, 2026 extends the term A and revolving maturities to `May 3, 2032` (`page:42`). The schedule therefore no longer matches the post-amendment structure for the term A and revolver amounts it places in 2028; the pro forma schedule is not supplied.

5. **Net debt basis.** The release defines net debt as `total debt, excluding premiums, discounts, and deferred financing expense, and the effect of foreign exchange that is economically hedged` less cash (`EX-99.1 Q3 page:20`); the 10-Q prints `Total debt` and `Total debt principal including accrued interest` on different bases (`10-Q Q3 page:26`). The three bases are not reconciled in the sources.

6. **Legal provision scope.** The 10-Q contingency note (`page:40`) gives a Fast Code provision of `$109 million (A$157.5 million)`, while the Adjusted EBITDA add-back for the quarter is `$105 million relates to a provision recognized to facilitate a potential resolution of the Fast Code Class Action, partially offset by an adjustment in connection with the Indian GST matter` (`page:16`). These are different scopes, not a conflict, and must not be added or substituted.

7. **Stated period labels.** Release highlights and the 10-Q use the same Q3 2026 figures for revenue and net loss (`3,874` and `(1,148)` on the Q3 10-Q `page:6` and release `page:22`). Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of `360` is a release figure (`EX-99.1 Q3 page:24`); the 10-Q segment note gives segment totals for the quarter and nine months (`10-Q Q3 page:14`).
### Evidence assessment by need

- **Statements and periods.** Evidence: the Q3 10-Q prints `Three months ended September 30, Nine months ended September 30,` columns for 2026 and 2025 (`page:6`), and the 10-K prints three fiscal years. Risk: the cash flow statement is nine months only, so quarterly cash items rest on the release's subtraction. Consequence: CP-1 can build discrete quarters for income items from the three 10-Qs and releases, and must label the derived cash-flow quarter as management-derived.

- **Debt and liquidity.** Evidence: the latest debt table lists every facility and note series with principal and carrying value; the revolver note states `The Group had an undrawn revolving credit commitment of $782 million (£590 million) as of September 30, 2026` and `$13 million (£10 million)` reserved for guarantees (`10-Q Q3 page:27`). Risk: the amendment text is only summarised, and letters of credit other than the guarantee reserve are not tabulated against the revolver. Consequence: CP-2 can compute liquidity at September 30, 2026 from printed inputs and must state the pro forma revolver as a subsequent event.

- **Claims outside debt.** Evidence: operating leases (`10-Q Q3 page:75`: `the Group had operating lease obligations of $559 million with $142 million payable within 12 months`), purchase obligations (`page:75`: `totaled $4,998 million`), bank guarantees (`page:38`: `The maximum amount of the guarantees as of September 30, 2026 was $620 million`), the Fox option (`10-K page:132`: `Fox has until December 2030 to exercise the Fox Option`; fair value `Fox Option liability — — 100 100` at `10-Q Q3 page:33`), redeemable non-controlling interests and litigation and tax matters (`10-Q Q3 pages 38 to 42`). Risk: the 10-K lease note describes `Substantially all leases are long-term operating leases` and the 10-Qs carry no lease maturity table. Consequence: CP-2 can set out these claims with their locators; lease maturities are available at December 31, 2025 only.

- **Latest quarter and after.** Evidence: Brazil operations are `currently ceased` after the measure announced `September 25, 2026` (`10-Q Q3 page:14`); the UKI restructuring plan of `October 20, 2026` (`page:42`); the amendment of `October 30, 2026` (`page:42`); a paused repurchase programme (`page:75`); revised 2026 guidance (`EX-99.1 Q3 page:12`). Risk: guidance is management's claim and the restructuring cost is an estimate range. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 can cover the events up to the cutoff; none is dated after November 5, 2026.
## Calculations

None. CP-0 performs no calculation, normalisation or reconciliation. Every figure quoted above is copied from the cited page with its original period and unit. No source-count or page-count figure is used as a readiness proxy: readiness rests on the located content listed in the source register and the evidence assessment.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| No executed credit agreement, indentures, officer's certificates or First Amendment and Restatement Agreement. Terms are known from filing summaries only. | Medium | CP-2 | Obtain the credit agreement, the amendment of October 30, 2026 and the indenture; until then state terms as summarised in the filings. |

| Covenant ratio values are not printed; only `the Group was in compliance with all debt covenants` (`10-Q Q3 page:27`). The pre-amendment level was 5.20:1 and the post-amendment first lien level is 5.70:1, with different definitions. | Medium | CP-2 | Obtain the covenant definitions and the compliance certificate; do not present the release leverage ratio as covenant headroom. |

| Guarantor list and the subsidiary list (Exhibit 21.1) are not supplied. | Medium | CP-2, CP-1A | Obtain Exhibit 21.1 and guarantor detail; describe guarantors only as "the Group and certain of its subsidiaries". |

| The Q3 debt table prints no interest rates, issuers, guarantors or security. Rates and security come from the 10-K at December 31, 2025. Whether any rate changed in 2026 is not shown for the term loans, other than the post-amendment margin range of 1.40% to 2.00% for term A and revolver loans. | Medium | CP-2 | Cite the 10-K for legacy terms, label them as of December 31, 2025, and state the post-amendment margin from the Q3 10-Q. |

| Pro forma maturity schedule after the amendment is not supplied; the Q3 schedule is pre-amendment. | Medium | CP-2 | Rebuild the schedule by moving term A and revolver amounts to May 2032 only after the amended principal amounts are confirmed (`€382 million of term A2 loans and $1,374 million of term A3 loans`, `10-Q Q3 page:42`). |
| Facility-size statements are not reconciled (release approximately $240m increase; 10-Q revolver $1.86 billion). | Low | CP-2 | Use the filing figures and flag the release figure as unreconciled. |

| Letters of credit are mentioned only inside the bank guarantee note (`third-party letter of credit facilities`, `10-Q Q3 page:38`), with a total guarantee amount and no split by facility. Whether any draws on the revolver is not stated; the only printed revolver deduction is a `$13 million (£10 million)` reservation for guarantees (`10-Q Q3 page:27`). | Low | CP-2 | State the reservation as the only printed deduction and the guarantee total as separate; do not infer further revolver usage. |

| Cash flows in the 10-Qs are year-to-date only; quarterly cash flows are management-derived in the release. The Q3 10-Q cash flow caption reads "decrease" over positive amounts. | Low | CP-1 | Use year-to-date figures from the filings and label release-derived quarters; take balances, not the caption, for direction. |

| Segment comparatives may have been recast for customer transfers between regions during 2026 (`beginning April 1, 2026, PokerStars’ North America operations formed part of the US region`, `10-Q Q3 page:14`). The sources do not say whether FY2025 segment figures were recast. | Medium | CP-1, CP-1A | Compare the 10-K FY2025 segment tables with the 2025 comparatives in the 10-Qs before any LTM segment build. |

| No Q4 2025 earnings release, no investor presentations, no market quotes and no peer data. The Q3 10-Q says the post-amendment margin depends on `corporate ratings from Moody’s, S&P and Fitch` (`page:42`), but no rating is stated in any source, and the context ratings field is blank. | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Treat market, rating and peer content as Not supplied. Ratings and the applicable margin are not inferred. |
| The extraction was not compared with the filed HTML or XBRL; no chart or image content was inspected. | Low | CP-5 | Spot-check key figures against filed statements in the verification step. |
| The context lists the country as Netherlands; the filings state Ireland. | Low | CP-1A | Use the filings; note the context field as inconsistent. |

| Fox option: the option price and fair value are disclosed, but the Fox option agreement is not supplied; the 10-K states the exercise window to December 2030. | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Treat as a contingent claim described in filings only. |

Conflicts logged with locators are listed under "Cross-source distinctions and conflicts" above, each with its downstream effect. No source is blocked, no duplicate source is present, and no draft or unsigned material is supplied. The pack holds three earnings releases but no duplicates of any filing.
## Next module

CP-1 runs next on the 10-K, the three 10-Qs and the releases. It should take the filings as controlling, label release-derived quarters, carry the unreconciled leverage and net debt bases above, and check the segment recast question before building any LTM view. CP-1A and CP-2 follow on the same sources, with CP-2 treating the October 30, 2026 amendment as a subsequent event described only in the Q3 10-Q and release. CP-5 verifies locators and carries the extraction-fidelity limit. The next evidence action is to obtain the credit agreement amendment, the indenture and the covenant definitions.

The CP-0 handoff was opened and used. It reports all four selected modules ready with limitations. This answer carries its limits forward: no executed credit documents, no covenant ratio values, the release leverage ratio and the covenant ratio use different definitions, and segment comparatives may not be recast. Where this answer settles a CP-0 question it says so under "Consistency with CP-0".
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,331 against total debt of 12,313 gives total leverage of 5.28x and net leverage of 4.55x at Q3 2026, up from 4.31x and 3.67x at FY2025. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is the company's own measure, not the covenant definition, and the last-twelve-month figure is calculated from filed annual and interim data. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was 1,499 against 2,013 a year earlier, with the US segment falling most. | Debt is almost unchanged, so lower earnings drive the rise in leverage. | High |

| Cash interest cover on last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 3.67x, against 5.36x for FY2025. | Cash interest paid rose to 636 as the 2025 acquisition debt carried a full year of interest. | Medium |

| Free cash flow is positive at 515 for the last twelve months, but 319 once player deposit movements are removed. | Share repurchases of 543 exceeded free cash flow before the programme was paused. | Medium |

| Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was cash of 1,708 plus undrawn revolver commitments of 782, down from 1,828 and 929 at FY2025. | Headroom narrowed before the October 2026 amendment enlarged the revolver. | High |

| Add-backs for legal provisions, restructuring and Brazil impairment sit outside Adjusted EBITDA, and covenant EBITDA is defined separately. | Covenant headroom cannot be measured from these sources. | Low |
### Financial base view

The consolidated financial base is complete enough to use: audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim sets, a segment note, an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation in every period and a debt note at each quarter end are all located. The picture they give is of a group whose total debt rose by 5,530 in 2025 (6,736 to 12,266, C13), with the proceeds of the 2025 term loan and note issues used to repay the bridge loans for the Snai acquisition and the Boyd transaction (10-K `page:126`), and whose earnings have since weakened. Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 is 1,499 against 2,013 for nine months 2025, driven by the US segment (241 against 612) and a higher UK gaming duty in International, while total debt is almost flat (12,313 at September 30, 2026 against 12,266 at December 31, 2025). Calculated total debt to Adjusted EBITDA therefore rises from 4.31x at FY2025 to 5.28x on a last-twelve-month basis, and the company's own net leverage ratio moves from 3.7x to 4.6x. Cash interest cover on the same basis falls from 5.36x to 3.67x.

Three features limit the view. First, the headline measure is the company's Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes share-based compensation, restructuring, legal loss contingencies, transaction costs and impairment; the 10-Q says its definition `may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt agreements`. Second, the last-twelve-month figures are calculated from annual and year-to-date data, and the segment comparatives for 2025 appear not to be recast for the 2026 customer transfers between regions. Third, cash flow from operations moves with player deposit balances, which are not the Group's own cash. The figures should be read as a documented reported base with calculated overlays, not as covenant tests.

The three 2026 quarters sum to the nine-month figures printed in the Q3 10-Q (Adjusted EBITDA 1,499; net loss 1,235), and the three 2025 quarters sum to 2,013 and a net loss of 417 (C8). Q3 2026 net loss includes a Brazil impairment of 873 and a legal loss contingency add-back of 105 (Q3 10-Q `page:72` and `page:73`).
### Definition review

- Adjusted EBITDA is defined in the Q3 10-Q as `income (loss) before income taxes; other (expense) income, net; interest expense, net; depreciation and amortization; transaction fees and associated costs; restructuring and integration costs; legal (settlements) loss contingencies; gaming tax disputes; impairment of property and equipment, intangible assets, right-of-use assets and goodwill; and share-based compensation charge` (`page:70`). The 10-K notes that `Beginning January 1, 2024, the Group revised its definition of Adjusted EBITDA` (`page:99`); FY2024 and FY2023 figures in the 10-K are on the revised basis, and no earlier basis is supplied.

- Items excluded in the nine months to September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:72`): share-based compensation 176, transaction fees 32, restructuring and integration costs 254, legal loss contingencies 200 and impairment 873. The restructuring programmes `are expected to run until 2029` (`page:73`), so the restructuring add-back is recurring in practice. Cash cost of the UKI restructuring, `$80 million to $90 million` pre-tax, is announced after quarter end (`page:42`) and is not in any period shown.

- Operating lease cost is inside Adjusted EBITDA (it is an operating expense), and operating lease liabilities sit outside debt. No finance lease balance is printed; the 10-K says `Substantially all leases are long-term operating leases` (`page:186`).

- Leverage definitions: the release defines `Leverage ratio is defined as net debt divided by last twelve months adjusted EBITDA` (Q3 release `page:21`). Its net debt adds back unamortized costs and removes unrealized foreign exchange on hedged debt (Q3 release `page:26`). This answer uses carrying total debt less unrestricted cash, so its net debt (10,605) is lower than the release's (10,656) by 51. The covenant ratio is `consolidated net borrowings to consolidated EBITDA as defined therein` with a limit of `5.20:1` before the October 30, 2026 amendment (10-K `page:128`) and a net first lien leverage level of `5.70:1.00` afterwards (Q3 10-Q `page:42`). No covenant ratio value is printed, so headroom is Not calculable.

- Cash interest paid is the supplemental cash flow line. It is not net of interest income (36 for 9M 2026 and 58 for 9M 2025 in the Q3 10-Q `page:19`), so interest cover on cash interest is stated before that income.

- Free cash flow follows the release definition (`Free cash flow is defined as net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less payments for property and equipment, intangible assets and capitalized software`, Q3 release `page:21`). Operating cash flow includes movements in player deposit liabilities and investments, which belong to players; the "excluding player deposit movements" rows remove them (C4).
### Reconciliations performed

- Segment to Group Adjusted EBITDA: FY2025 3,124 less overhead 279 equals 2,845 (10-K `page:168`); 9M 2026 1,739 less 240 equals 1,499; 9M 2025 2,226 less 213 equals 2,013 (Q3 10-Q `page:14`). Each equals the Group figure in the MD&A reconciliation (Q3 10-Q `page:72`).
- Reconciliation to net loss: the 9M 2026 add-backs listed on Q3 10-Q `page:72` take net loss of 1,235 to Adjusted EBITDA of 1,499 (C9).

- Debt: the Q3 debt note total (12,313) equals 170 current plus 12,143 non-current on the balance sheet (Q3 10-Q `page:6`, `page:26`); the eleven instrument rows sum to 12,390 of principal including accrued interest (C10).
- Release net debt: 12,313 + 77 − 26 − 1,708 = 10,656, matching Q3 release `page:26` (C10).

- Cash: opening 3,832, net movement 137 and foreign exchange (49) give 3,920, equal to unrestricted cash 1,708, restricted cash 95 and player deposit cash 2,117 (Q3 10-Q `page:9` and `page:10`). The caption on the movement line says "decrease" over a positive amount; the balances, not the caption, are used.

- Release leverage ratios: net debt on the release basis divided by calculated LTM Adjusted EBITDA gives 3.70x (Q1), 4.28x (Q2) and 4.57x (Q3), which round to the 3.7x, 4.3x and 4.6x the releases print (C11). This supports the LTM Adjusted EBITDA built here.
### Evidence assessment

- **Leverage.** Evidence: total debt 12,313 at September 30, 2026 against 12,266 at December 31, 2025 (`Total debt 12,313 12,266`, Q3 10-Q `page:26`), while LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 2,331 against 2,845. Mechanism: the 2025 acquisition debt is in place for the full period, and earnings fell in the US segment (241 against 612 for nine months) and from the UK gaming duty in International (Q3 10-Q `page:70`: `an increase of remote gaming tax in UK`). Consequence: calculated total leverage rose by about one turn between FY2025 and Q3 2026, and the company itself targets `2.0 - 2.5x` (Q3 release `page:12`).

- **Cover.** Evidence: cash interest paid 636 over the last twelve months against 531 in FY2025. Mechanism: a full year of interest on the notes due 2031 and Term Loan B due 2032 issued in 2025 (Q3 10-Q `page:53`: `a full quarter of interest on the Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and the USD First Lien Term Loan B due 2032 issued in August 2025`). Consequence: cover on cash interest fell from 5.36x to 3.67x, and the next twelve months carry `$696 million payable within 12 months net of hedging` of scheduled interest (Q3 10-Q `page:74`).

- **Cash flow.** Evidence: free cash flow of 377 for 9M 2026 against 269 for 9M 2025, but 201 against 396 once player deposit movements are removed. Mechanism: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was lifted by player funds (176) and higher accrued legal and gaming duty liabilities (Q3 10-Q `page:76`). Consequence: the improvement in reported free cash flow is not evidence of stronger underlying cash generation; share repurchases of 543 over the last twelve months exceeded free cash flow of 515, and the programme is now paused (Q3 10-Q `page:75`).

- **Liquidity.** Evidence: cash 1,708 and undrawn revolver commitments 782 at September 30, 2026. Mechanism: the revolver was drawn to fund operations and repayments (`drew £1,208 million ($1,621 million)`, Q3 10-Q `page:27`). Consequence: the sterling revolver headroom fell from 1,185 at March 31, 2026 to 782; the post-amendment commitment is larger, but its undrawn amount is not supplied.

- **Earnings quality.** Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,499 for 9M 2026 against an operating loss of 1,256 and net loss of 1,235. Mechanism: impairment of 873 on Brazil, legal loss contingencies of 200 and restructuring of 254 are excluded. Consequence: cash costs among those items (legal settlements, restructuring severance) will reduce free cash flow in later periods even though they do not reduce Adjusted EBITDA.

- **Guidance context (management claim).** The Q3 release gives 2026 guidance midpoints of revenue `$17.61bn` and Adjusted EBITDA `$2.495bn` (`page:12`). Subtracting the nine-month figures implies fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of about 996 and revenue of about 5,106 (C12). This is management's guidance, not a forecast built here, and it assumes the nine-month figures in this answer.
### Consistency with CP-0

- CP-0 asked whether FY2025 segment figures were recast for 2026 customer transfers. The Q3 10-Q MD&A describes `the migration of PokerStars North America to the U.S. segment` as an element of the period-over-period change (`page:69`), which indicates 2025 comparatives are as originally reported. Segment trends here therefore mix organic change with the transfers, and the effect is not quantified in the sources.

- CP-0 noted year-to-date cash flows only in the 10-Qs. This answer uses year-to-date data for LTM building and shows the release-derived quarter only for Q3 2026 free cash flow (35, Q3 release `page:27`).
- No CP-0 statement is corrected.
## Calculations
All inputs are reported values at the locators shown. LTM means FY2025 minus the 2025 comparative period plus the 2026 period.

FCF = operating cash flow − capex: 1,602 − 661; 1,184 − 777; 756 − 487; 904 − 527; LTM 1,332 − 817. FCF excluding player funds 696; 514; 396; 201; 319 |

Pre-amendment net total leverage limit 5.20:1 and post-amendment net first lien leverage level 5.70:1.00 are the only terms. | Medium | Leverage, covenant work | Obtain the credit agreement definitions and compliance certificate. |

| Player deposit movements inside operating cash flow are not Group cash. The treatment here removes them from operating cash flow; the release's own "excluding player funds" measure is given for Q3 2026 only (`(91)` against `(117)` for the quarter, Q3 release `page:27`) and also deducts extended-payment intangible purchases. | Medium | Free cash flow | Use the excluding-player-funds rows; do not mix with the release measure. |

| Legal, tax and contingent claims (Fast Code class action, Indian GST demand, IRS notices, Austrian and German player claims) and the Fox option are outside this financial base. | Medium | Claims outside debt | Cover in the debt and claims module. |
| Text extraction only; no comparison to filed HTML or XBRL. | Low | All figures | Spot-check key lines in verification. |
## Next module

CP-1A runs next on the business description and the same sources, and CP-2 follows with the debt structure, claims outside debt and the October 30, 2026 amendment. Both should take from this answer the calculated LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 2,331, total debt of 12,313, cash of 1,708, the pre-amendment liquidity and maturity profile, the distinction between company-defined and covenant leverage, and the open segment-recast question. This answer adds no figure of its own to those.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Flutter is an online betting group with no identified sponsor or controlling owner, earning 43% of FY2025 revenue in the US and 57% in International. Debt-funded 2025 acquisitions, UK tax rises and the Brazil ban now pressure leverage. | Medium | No credit documents, ownership schedule or investor presentations are supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Revenue is spread across the US and many International markets, and 88% of FY2025 revenue was online. | Diversification cushions single-market shocks, but regulatory and tax changes move earnings quickly. | High |

| UK remote gaming duty rose from 21% to 40% in April 2026, and Brazil banned online betting on September 25, 2026. | Margins and earnings fall in the affected markets, and Brazil assets were impaired. | High |
| 2025 acquisitions of Snai, NSX and the Boyd stake in FanDuel were financed with new debt. | Leverage rose, and management has paused share repurchases to deleverage. | High |
| Fox holds an option to buy 18.6% of FanDuel units until December 2030. | A sale would bring cash but cut the Group's FanDuel stake and could add consent rights. | Medium |

| The October 2026 credit agreement amendment extends maturities to May 2032 and changes the leverage covenant. | Near-term maturity pressure eases, but covenant terms cannot be checked against the executed document. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Flutter is an Ireland-incorporated, New York-headquartered online sports betting and iGaming group whose shares trade on the NYSE, with no sponsor and no controlling shareholder identified in the pack. Its revenue base is large and diversified by geography and product, with about 88% of FY2025 revenue earned online and the rest mainly through retail shops in the UK, Ireland, Italy and Serbia. Sportsbook revenue depends on the margin Flutter earns on fixed-odds bets, so it moves with sports results and with the sporting calendar; iGaming revenue is less dependent on the calendar. Both are exposed to gaming taxes that governments change at short notice, and the last year shows how fast this transmits: the UK raised remote gaming duty sharply in April 2026, Brazil's executive ban closed Flutter's Brazilian operations within days in September 2026, and India's 2025 ban ended Junglee. In India and Brazil Flutter took impairments, and in the UK it announced a restructuring.

The transaction history matters more to a creditor than the operating model. In 2025 the Group bought Snai in Italy, a 56% stake in NSX in Brazil, and the 5% of FanDuel held by Boyd, funding them with bridge loans refinanced by new term loan B and senior secured notes issued in June and August 2025. Total debt rose as a result (CP-1), while Brazil, bought with NSX in May 2025, was shut down within sixteen months and carries a large impairment. Management has since paused share repurchases to prioritise deleveraging and set a target leverage range, but earnings fell in 2026 and leverage is well above that range (CP-1). The contingent claim of Fox on FanDuel, a new CEO from October 1, 2026, a UKI restructuring and a credit agreement amendment on October 30, 2026 are subsequent changes that the debt and covenant modules must treat as post-period events. The amendment is known only from filing summaries.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Evidence and locator | Credit mechanic and implication |

| Business | Online sports betting and iGaming operator with sportsbook, iGaming and other products (exchange, pari-mutuel, daily fantasy sports, prediction markets). | Documentary Fact | `These products are offered by FanDuel (sportsbook, iGaming and other products), Sky Betting & Gaming (sportsbook and iGaming products), Sportsbet (sportsbook products), PokerStars (iGaming products)` (10-K `page:8`) | Many brands in many regulatory regimes spread licence and tax risk, but each market has its own cost of sales and tax rate. |

| Scale claim | The Group describes itself as the largest operator by revenue. | Management Language | `Flutter is the world’s leading online sports betting and iGaming operator based on revenue.` (10-K `page:8`) | Scale supports marketing efficiency and negotiating power; the claim is management's and not independently verified here. |

| Product mix | Sportsbook is the largest product, iGaming second, and most revenue is online. | Documentary Fact | `For fiscal 2025, 53% of our revenue was derived from sportsbook, 44% of our revenue was derived from iGaming, and 3% of our revenue was derived from other products, while 88% of our revenue at the Group level was generated from our online businesses.` (10-K `page:10`) | Sportsbook revenue carries outcome variance; iGaming is steadier but more heavily taxed in some markets. |

| Revenue model | Sportsbook earns a spread on fixed odds; iGaming earns hold; poker and exchange earn rake or commission. | Documentary Fact | `We generate revenue by setting odds in a manner that includes a theoretical spread to be earned on each contest less winnings paid and expenses associated with promotional activity.` (10-K `page:10`) | Revenue is exposed to sports results in any period, so a run of customer-favourable results reduces earnings without changing volumes. |

| Geographic mix | Two reportable segments: US and International. | Documentary Fact | `The U.S. segment is our fastest growing and our largest region, constituting $6,967 million (or 43%) of our revenue for fiscal 2025.` (10-K `page:11`); `Our International segment constituted $9,416 million (or 57%) of our revenue for fiscal 2025.` (10-K `page:11`) | International carries the larger share of earnings; the US is the growth and investment segment, so the two segments pull Adjusted EBITDA in different directions (CP-1: US 241 against 612 for nine months). |

| International regions | UKI, Southern Europe and Africa, Asia Pacific, CEE, Brazil and other regions. | Documentary Fact | `Our UKI region constituted $3,547 million (or 22%) of our Group total revenue for fiscal 2025.` (10-K `page:12`); `Our Brazil region constituted $227 million (or 1%) of our Group total revenue for fiscal 2025.` (10-K `page:12`) | The UK is the largest single international tax exposure; Brazil was small in revenue terms, so the ban's direct revenue loss is limited even though the impairment was large. |

| Retail | Retail betting shops complement online. | Documentary Fact | `Our online operations are complemented by 1,127 retail shops, mainly in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy and Serbia.` (10-K `page:10`) | A small fixed-cost retail base; closures in the UKI restructuring would reduce fixed costs but not remove the UK tax. |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

In 2025 Flutter completed three acquisitions. On April 30, 2025 it bought 100% of Pluto (Italia) S.p.A, the holding company of Snai, for approximately `$2.6 billion (€2.3 billion)` (Q3 10-Q `page:25`). On May 14, 2025 it acquired a 56% interest in NSX for `$674 million (BRL 3,799 million)` with call and put options over the remainder (10-K `page:9`). It also acquired the 5% redeemable non-controlling interest in FanDuel held by Boyd for `$1,553 million`, taking its holding to 100% subject to the Fox option (10-K `page:9`). The accounting for Snai and NSX was finalised in the second quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:25`, `page:26`). All three are documentary facts with status completed. The sources give acquisition terms only in these summaries, and no acquisition agreements are supplied.

The acquisitions were financed in stages. A `€2.5 billion` bridge term loan drawn on April 29, 2025 funded Snai, and a `$1.75 billion` bridge drawn on July 30, 2025 funded the Boyd transaction (10-K `page:125`, `page:126`). They were repaid with new `$1,250 million` of Term Loan B due June 4, 2032 (`$750 million` on June 4 and `$500 million` on August 7, 2025) and with the 2031 senior secured notes issued in the same two tranches: `$1,625 million of 5.875%`, `€850 million of 4.000%` and `£700 million of 6.125%` (10-K `page:126`, `page:127`, `page:128`). The 2029 notes of `$525 million` at 6.375% and `€500 million` at 5.000% had been issued by Flutter Treasury DAC on April 29, 2024 (10-K `page:127`). The use of proceeds was repayment of the bridges, general corporate purposes and costs (10-K `page:126`). Liquidity effect: the debt table shows total debt rising over 2025 (CP-1), and the Group states it believes it has sufficient capacity through cash, internal funds and the revolver (Q3 10-Q `page:74`, a management statement).

After the quarter, on October 30, 2026, the Group signed the First Amendment and Restatement Agreement to the November 2023 credit agreement (Q3 10-Q `page:42`). It extends the term A and revolver maturities to `May 3, 2032`, raises the revolver commitment to `$1.86 billion` with a US dollar base currency, redenominates term A into `€382 million of term A2 loans and $1,374 million of term A3 loans`, replaces the net total leverage covenant with a net first lien leverage covenant at `5.70:1.00`, and prices term A and revolver loans at a margin of `1.40% to 2.00%` set by corporate ratings (Q3 10-Q `page:42`). The revolver increase took effect on November 3, 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:74`). Status: completed, a subsequent event after September 30, 2026, described only in a note and in the Q3 release (`page:12`); the executed document is not supplied. The liquidity effect is an enlarged revolver, but the undrawn amount after the amendment is not disclosed. The Q3 release describes the facility increase as approximately `$240m` for the refinanced facilities without defining the set, which is not reconciled to the revolver figure (see conflicts).

Other transactions and structural changes: the Group delisted from the LSE on August 3, 2026 (Q2 10-Q `page:37`); it paused the share repurchase programme during Q3 2026 (`paused the 2024 Share Repurchase Program to prioritize deleveraging`, Q3 10-Q `page:75`), having repurchased shares under the `$5 billion` authorisation (Q3 10-Q `page:75`); on October 20, 2026 it committed to a UKI restructuring plan affecting up to `1,400 employees` with charges of `$80 million to $90 million` (Q3 10-Q `page:42`); and Brazil operations were closed in September and October 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:14`). There is no sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation and no disposal described in the sources. No new debt issue is described after the October 30, 2026 amendment, and nothing is dated after the cutoff of November 5, 2026.
### Governance, capital allocation and creditor behaviour
| Documented action | Category | Behaviour reading | Mechanic | Evidence and locator |

| Debt-funded acquisitions in 2025 (Snai, NSX, Boyd stake) | Documentary Fact | Neutral or Mixed | Acquisitions lifted debt and then leverage; the Group states that Snai and NSX were finalised in Q2 2026. Whether synergies appear is not evidenced. | `The acquisition of Snai was funded by the net proceeds from the issuance of the Senior Notes due 2031, and the Term Loan B due 2032 borrowings` (Q3 10-Q `page:25`) |

| Share repurchases while leverage was rising, then paused | Documentary Fact | Neutral or Mixed, moving to Supportive | Repurchases used cash that could have repaid debt; the pause redirects cash to deleveraging. Stated intent only; cash effect arrives in later periods. | `paused the 2024 Share Repurchase Program to prioritize deleveraging` (Q3 10-Q `page:75`); `Prioritizing organic investment and deleveraging; share repurchase program paused for the foreseeable future` (Q3 release `page:1`) |

| Stated leverage target | Management Language | Supportive (stated, not yet achieved) | A target range gives a reference for deleveraging policy, but timing is open-ended. | `We are committed to returning within our target leverage range of 2.0 - 2.5x over the medium-term` (Q3 release `page:12`) |

| Transparent reporting | Documentary Fact | Supportive | Quarterly detail on debt, segments and subsequent events; but the 10-K discloses prior material weaknesses, since remediated. | `While no material weaknesses were identified as of December 31, 2025` (10-K `page:84`) |

| Fox option and consent rights | Documentary Fact | Insufficient Information on willingness | The Group and Fox may interpret rights differently, so a future sale could limit actions the Group wishes to take, including financing. | `Fox’s interpretation of its rights in relation to the Fox Option may differ from that of Flutter.` (10-K `page:30`) |

| Priming, uptiering, drop-downs, non-pro-rata exchanges, collateral release | Insufficient Information | Not assessable | No such action is described in the sources. Legal capacity under the indenture and credit agreement cannot be tested because neither is supplied. Absence of evidence is not a favourable conclusion. | Not applicable: no source describes any such action |

Legal capacity (what the documents permit) is not assessable from the pack; willingness is shown by the documented repurchase pause and acquisition funding; feasibility is addressed by CP-1 (leverage and liquidity at Q3 2026) and CP-2.
